date_note: Day the company announced the leak, per Daily SECU; the abnormal access ran from 4 to 6 November.
title: Welcome Payments says abnormal access to its merchant admin page leaked customer data
summary: Daily SECU reports that Welcome Payments announced a leak of payment-service users' data after abnormal access to its merchant admin page from 4 November 11:00 to 6 November 08:00. A second notice on 24 November corrected the scale from 1,388 to 1,326 cases (건). The company says card numbers, passwords, expiry dates and CVC were not leaked and the leaked data alone cannot enable unauthorized payments.
plain: Daily SECU reports Welcome Payments told users that data such as names, phone numbers and payment details leaked via its merchant admin page. The company says card numbers and CVC codes were not leaked. The scale is 1,326 cases.
exec: A Korean payment gateway says abnormal access to its merchant admin page exposed payment-service users' data, now put at 1,326 cases; the company says card numbers were not leaked.

evidence.quote: 24일 웰컴페이먼츠는 지난 17일 오후 가맹점 관리자를 통해 개인 및 신용 정보가 유출됐으며 당시 1388건 정보가 유출됐다고 봤으나 다시 파악한 결과 1326건으로 줄었다고 밝혔다.
웰컴페이먼츠는 지난 11월 20일 개인정보 유출 사실을 공지한 데 이어 24일 오전 8시 35분 2차 안내를 통해 유출 규모를 기존 1,388건에서 1,326건으로 정정했다.
지난 11월 4일 오전 11시부터 6일 오전 8시까지 가맹점 관리자 페이지에 대한 비정상 접근이 발생했다.

validation.note: Corroborated by two independent publishers, dailysecu.com (Daily SECU) and zdnet.co.kr (ZDNet Korea), each relaying the company's statement of the leak and the revision from 1,388 to 1,326 cases. They differ on timing: Daily SECU gives abnormal access 4 to 6 November; ZDNet Korea says the leak was via the merchant administrator on 'the 17th' (지난 17일 오후). The company's notices were not read.

review.note: Compared access window, 1,388 to 1,326 correction, not-leaked data and dates against Daily SECU; evidence quotes found
